forecasts.question: Will the Knesset pass the dissolution bill's final reading with a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27 before EOD 2026-07-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: Cold-start audit (Sunday July 12): p_inherited=0.45, p_cold=0.05, gap=40pp — Judge selects cold-start p=0.05. Knesset legal adviser Sagit Afik formally recommended July 17 as dissolution date (2 days after the July 15 horizon) and October 27 as the election date. Both resolution conditions fail simultaneously: (a) final reading scheduled July 17, not before July 15 EOD; (b) election date October 27 triggers ambiguity_rule 'date on/after Oct 27 = NO.' No extraordinary session before July 15 is scheduled.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset passes the dissolution bill in final (third) reading AND that passage specifies a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27, before EOD 2026-07-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two TIER1 (Times of Israel/Reuters/AP/JPost) citing the Knesset plenum vote record.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary/first/second readings without final passage do NOT count; passage that leaves the date to a later committee or sets only a band without a fixed date = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; if a fixed date on/after 27 Oct is set, resolve NO.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: Cold-start audit (Sunday July 12): p_inherited=0.35, p_cold=0.88, gap=53pp — Judge selects cold-start p=0.88. The dissolution bill passed first reading 106-0 (all coalition and opposition parties). Knesset legal adviser Sagit Afik formally recommended July 17 as the dissolution date, before the October 27 horizon. Under resolution_criteria: 'Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27' — the July 17 dissolution process constitutes early dissolution before Oct 27. Latest polls: Eisenkot Yashar 23 seats, Likud 20 (Haaretz July 9); opposition bloc projects 69 vs. coalition 51.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.

forecasts.question: Will the Knesset formally dissolve (complete second and third readings of dissolution bill and issue dissolution proclamation) before EOD 2026-07-20?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. Legal adviser recommended July 17 dissolution date; first reading 106-0 with all coalition parties; scheduling confirmed. Risk scenarios for NO: Supreme Court injunction, haredi faction dispute over bill text, or procedural delay beyond July 20.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset completes second and third readings of the dissolution bill AND the Knesset Speaker formally proclaims dissolution, confirmed by Knesset official record or government gazette, before EOD 2026-07-20.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record (knesset.gov.il), Times of Israel, Jerusalem Post, Haaretz. Official Knesset proclamation or Speaker statement required.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If second and third readings pass but formal dissolution proclamation issued after July 20 due to procedural lag = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Bill passage without proclamation = NO. Court-ordered stay pending review = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.expected_effect: Passage before July 20 resolves YES; postponement past July 20 resolves NO

indicators.expected_effect: Procedural alignment with July 17; necessary not sufficient for YES

forecasts.question: Will the June 17 US-Iran MOU framework remain formally in effect (not publicly suspended or terminated by either party) through EOD 2026-08-12?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. p set at 0.40 (reduced from initial 0.50 per DA partial-accept): IRGC maritime attacks July 6-7 triggered US retaliatory strikes; Hormuz transits fell to 11/day by July 10; Araghchi publicly stated US threats impede a final agreement. MOU faces severe stress but no formal government-level termination statement confirmed as of July 12. Counterweights: Doha back-channel (Qatar, Pakistan mediators active), both parties' economic stakes in Hormuz commerce, MOU provides structured de-escalation format.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if neither the US nor Iran has issued an official government statement formally suspending, abrogating, or declaring the June 17 MOU null and void by EOD 2026-08-12, AND at least one technical-level engagement under the MOU framework has been confirmed by a TIER1 source during July 12 to August 12.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1: Reuters, AP, CNN, Al Jazeera. Official US: White House press office or State Dept. Official Iran: IRNA, Iranian foreign ministry statement. Both required for formal termination determination.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Conditional suspension pending a specific demand (not formal termination) = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-YES. Both parties silent with no meetings AND no formal termination = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-YES. Unilateral IRGC action without government-level MOU termination statement does not alone trigger NO.

indicators.expected_effect: Escalation episode; absent government-level termination, does not alone resolve NO

indicators.expected_effect: Rhetorical warning, not formal suspension; monitoring for escalation to official termination language

forecasts.question: Will the Strait of Hormuz 7-day average commercial transit count reach 40 or more vessels per day before EOD 2026-09-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. Current transit level 11/day as of July 10, down from 35 on July 7 following IRGC attacks on three commercial vessels and US retaliatory strikes. Pre-crisis baseline ~90/day. UK/France multinational MCM mission announced July 6, not yet commenced. Expert estimates: 40-50 days sustained MCM required before insurance companies restore coverage. Recovery to 40/day (44% of baseline) requires both sustained MCM and no further IRGC interdiction over 65 days.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if any TIER1 or named AIS source (IMF PortWatch, UANI Iran Shipping Updates, Windward AI, Lloyd's List) records a consecutive 7-day window achieving a commercial transit average of 40 or more vessels per day through the Strait of Hormuz before EOD 2026-09-15. Naval vessels do not count toward the commercial threshold.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1/OSINT: IMF PortWatch (portwatch.imf.org), UANI Iran Shipping Updates, Windward Daily Intelligence. At least one named outlet confirming the 7-day average required; single-day counts not sufficient.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: AIS-dark vessels do not count. Naval-escorted civilian convoys count only if the commercial vessels themselves are confirmed transiting. If PortWatch data unavailable, require two independent AIS sources. Single-day count of 40+ without confirmed 7-day average = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: UK/France multinational MCM mission commences
indicators.expected_effect: Commencement necessary but not sufficient for recovery to 40/day by Sep 15; requires sustained 40+ days of clearance

indicators.name: IRGC maritime attack recurrence
indicators.expected_effect: Any recurrence would likely extend closure timeline beyond Sep 15

forecasts.question: Will the US and Iran sign a comprehensive binding final agreement (substantively beyond the June 17 MOU, covering at minimum nuclear limits and sanctions) before EOD 2026-10-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. Active obstacles: MOU 60-day window expires approximately August 17; Hormuz transits near-standstill after July 6-7 attacks; Araghchi on record that US threats impede final agreement; hardline Mojtaba Khamenei faction blocking Ghalibaf's diplomatic concessions; JCPOA formally terminated, UN sanctions reinstated; US demands on missiles and proxies not addressed in MOU. No principals-level meeting confirmed since July 1 Doha session.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source confirms that the US and Iran formally signed a comprehensive bilateral agreement (by any name) that addresses at minimum: (a) specific uranium enrichment limits or dismantlement commitments and (b) a defined sanctions relief architecture, with the agreement publicly acknowledged by both governments.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1: Reuters, AP, BBC, CNN. Confirmed by both White House press office AND official Iranian government statement (IRNA or foreign ministry statement) within the same news cycle.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: An MOU extension without a comprehensive final agreement covering both nuclear and sanctions = NO. A partial deal on one topic only (e.g., Hormuz navigation alone) = NO. A deal acknowledged by one party but not the other = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. A framework agreement setting deadlines for future negotiations without binding commitments = NO.

indicators.name: Araghchi US-threats impediment statement
indicators.expected_effect: Explicit obstacle to deal; not itself termination but narrows deal space

indicators.name: MOU 60-day window expires approx Aug 17
indicators.expected_effect: Creates hard deadline; if MOU expires without extension or deal, YES probability drops further

indicators.name: Technical talks under MOU framework
indicators.expected_effect: Necessary but insufficient; no high-level meetings reported since July 1 Doha session

forecasts.question: Will Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party hold a seat projection equal to or greater than Likud's in the average of published Israeli election polls through EOD 2026-09-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. Haaretz July 9 reported first poll where Eisenkot's Yashar (23 seats) exceeded Likud (20 seats) outright; Channel 12 July 7 showed both at 23. PM preference: Eisenkot 43% vs. Netanyahu 39% (Channel 13). Bennett Together at 15 seats. Opposition bloc projects 69 seats vs. coalition 51. Netanyahu exploring adding Smotrich to Likud reserved list amid fears Religious Zionist Party may fall below 3.25% electoral threshold.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the simple average of the three most recently published seat-projection polls (by any TIER1 Israeli outlet) as of EOD 2026-09-01 shows Yashar with a projected seat count equal to or greater than Likud's projected seat count. If fewer than three polls published between Aug 1 and Sep 1, use all available polls in that window.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1: Haaretz, Times of Israel, Jerusalem Post. Polling firms: Channel 12, Channel 13, Maariv, Panels Politics.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If Yashar and Likud tie in the average, resolve YES. If Eisenkot merges Yashar with another party before Sep 1, use the combined merged-party projection vs. Likud. If Netanyahu removed from Likud list and Likud rebrands or merges = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If fewer than two polls available = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.expected_effect: Current baseline at or above parity; trajectory Eisenkot gaining over past 4 weeks
